scope.operation: Verify all six concrete DRW_Surface subtypes survive named-BLOCK DXF export and callback staging/readback.
behavior: A generated named BLOCK contains PLANESURFACE, EXTRUDEDSURFACE, REVOLVEDSURFACE, SWEPTSURFACE, LOFTEDSURFACE, and NURBSURFACE entities copied with their concrete C++ runtime types.
ASCII and Binary DXF output is read through dx_iface::fileImport with applyExtrusion=false and direct dxfRW::read with applyExtrusion=true.

Readback checks the unique named BLOCK, six ordered entity types, concrete runtime subtypes, common isoline/modeler-version values, and subtype-only field sentinels for the five derived payload types.

coverage: Generated ASCII and Binary named-BLOCK surface export/readback.
Raw-frame fileImport and applyExtrusion direct-reader callback staging.
Concrete subtype identity and subtype-specific field sentinels for six surface families.
Selected typed/raw callback ordering and retained deep-copy lifetime after parser/queue teardown and same-facade reuse.
ASCII/Binary and extended/non-extended modes for generated BLOCK and non-BLOCK event sequences.
Malformed ENDBLK variants publish no staged children and corrected reads retry on the same reader.
Known and non-standard callback exceptions preserve the primary exception, balance BLOCK/ENDBLK once, and permit retry; cleanup-only exceptions propagate.

limitations: This is generated transport evidence only. It does not establish physical producer breadth, exhaustive BLOCK callback coverage, typed/raw ordering, owned-copy lifetime, ENDBLK publication behavior, replay-exception cleanup, native surface semantics, B-rep validity, or ACIS/ACDS support.
No external DWG/DXF fixture or public callback/interface change was added.
